channel.title: Diffbrief · Security
channel.description: Daily security stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Danfoss AK-SM800A controllers face multiple remote-code-execution flaws
item.description: The excerpt reports attacks against internet-exposed Danfoss and Copeland fridge controllers, with remote code execution among the Danfoss AK-SM800A flaws. It underscores the risks of exposing operational equipment directly to the internet.

item.title: PostgreSQL type confusion turns into reliable memory-corruption exploitation
item.description: Changing a field's type after storing a composite value led to a new class of PostgreSQL type-confusion bugs and reliable memory corruption. A flaw in database core is relevant to engineers operating PostgreSQL, including in managed environments.

item.title: Defender logs showed 217 sample submissions, including unreleased software
item.description: A developer found 217 Defender sample-submission events over three months; MpCmdRun.exe uploaded 224 MB to Azure storage in one day, and event 2050 recorded filenames and hashes. The investigation gives engineers concrete visibility into endpoint sample uploads and the logs used to inspect them.

item.title: Glasswing findings outnumber fixes, with duplicates and withdrawals adding to triage
item.description: A VulnCheck review says 217 of 7,349 public Glasswing findings are marked fixed, while 1,654 are duplicates and 419 withdrawn. The figures raise questions about AI-assisted vulnerability triage and the burden placed on maintainers.

item.title: GitHub Actions lockfiles let workflows use version tags instead of SHA pins
item.description: A GitHub CLI extension locks workflows so they can reference version tags rather than manually pinned commit SHAs, which are safer against mutable-tag attacks. This offers a concrete way to manage CI supply-chain risk.

item.title: Apache HTTP/2 race condition can corrupt heap memory and enable RCE
item.description: A race in mod_http2's assign_headers() can let unauthenticated remote attackers corrupt heap memory and achieve code execution; the excerpt reports no exploit or in-the-wild attacks. Apache operators should assess exposure and follow the project's advisory for mitigation.

item.title: glibc considers tunables to block programs built without ASLR support
item.description: After a buffer overflow in Node.js’s Brotli decoder exposed that official Linux binaries could not use ASLR, glibc is considering tunables to forbid programs without ASLR support. The proposal offers a hardening path for widely deployed software, though it may not address the root cause.

item.title: llm 0.37.2 fixes cases that could expose configured API keys
item.description: The release fixes two cases where LLM could send a configured OpenAI API key to another provider: an unstored key name and a responses model run with the chat-completions option. Teams using compatible endpoints should update and review their configuration.

item.title: GKE ClusterNetworkPolicy applies tiered network controls across a cluster
item.description: ClusterNetworkPolicy uses admin, network-policy, and baseline tiers to apply cluster-wide rules, including controls for traffic to an LLM and blocking metadata access. The tier model is useful for engineers enforcing security boundaries across inference workloads.

item.title: Anti-unification and e-graphs expose meaningful differences in formal policies
item.description: An open-source engine uses anti-unification over an e-graph to identify shared policy structure and preserve differing expressions for review, using supplied algebraic and domain rules. This can make policy changes easier to audit than noisy textual diffs.

item.title: A macOS Secure Enclave SSH setup works, but the author switched to Secretive
item.description: The author found a native macOS Secure Enclave approach for SSH keys functional but unsatisfactory, and later switched to Secretive for a better prompt. The account is relevant to engineers weighing key protection against developer usability.

item.title: Gemini may send personal Drive and email content to human reviewers
item.description: Google's updated guidance says connected files and emails from consumer accounts can enter human-review pipelines; Workspace commercial accounts are governed separately. Engineers building AI products should account for account scope and make data-review boundaries explicit.

item.title: Anthropic-attributed CVEs outnumber recorded fixes in Project Glasswing data
item.description: VulnCheck counts 442 attributed CVEs, 217 marked fixed and only two identified as exploited; it also reports a widening gap between new findings and fixes. The figures raise practical questions about validation, disclosure and remediation capacity in AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.

item.title: YubiKey, TPM and Secure Enclave can keep SSH keys off disk
item.description: The author describes using hardware-backed options to avoid storing unprotected SSH key material on disk, while noting that passphrase-protected keys may be sufficient for many threat models. Engineers can compare the added protection with their existing SSH key practices.

item.title: Rust std and core have unsafe-code paths that can trigger UB from safe Rust
item.description: Microsoft’s FORGE Lab reports standard-library issues involving misplaced trust in panic behavior, user implementations and the underlying system, found with an AI-powered scanner. The findings highlight how unsafe internals can undermine safe APIs and where library audits need to look.

item.title: Psalm 7 adds default security analysis and faster taint tracking
item.description: Psalm 7 enables security analysis by default, adds taint flows for LLM prompt and URL injection, and claims 10x-plus performance. Its expanded PHP analysis and side-effect model matter to teams securing large codebases.

item.title: Attackers used Qubole-linked credentials to enter customer AWS environments
item.description: An actor used credentials tied to Qubole to assume customer-trusted AWS roles, enumerate resources, collect secrets and access S3 data across multiple environments; the investigation offers hunting and exposure-reduction guidance. Cloud teams should review third-party IAM trust and investigate credentials exposed through vendor integrations.

item.title: Deno’s permission model may give a misleading sense of security
item.description: The essay examines Deno’s permissions system, which limits runtime access such as file reads and shell commands. It frames a security-model critique, though the excerpt does not include the author’s specific arguments or evidence.

item.title: Chained Prusa printer flaws enabled network-delivered code execution
item.description: The researcher reports 14 findings, roughly 23 defects, and a chain that let network-sent code run on the printer's main controller; Prusa fixed the findings in Buddy firmware above 7.0.0. It is a detailed security case with a clear update action, though limited to a specific printer line.

item.title: Rails Active Storage flaw can enable unauthenticated file writes and possible code execution
item.description: The critical flaw affects Rails apps using ImageMagick to process Active Storage attachments; crafted uploads can write arbitrary files and, under some configurations, read sensitive files or reach remote code execution. Teams should check exposure and prioritize a Rails security update or the offered patch.

item.title: Web frameworks may trust Forwarded headers that proxies pass through unchanged
item.description: Rails, Spring and Jetty may use Forwarded values by default, while many proxies and middleware leave client-supplied values untouched. Engineers should audit proxy-to-application header trust, since untrusted values can influence how applications interpret requests.

item.title: Connected-car security research finds a path to remote unlocking across a major brand
item.description: The investigation traces the automaker's connected-car app to the internet-facing services involved in remote unlocking. It is a reminder that connected products' security depends on the backend infrastructure as well as vehicle hardware.

item.title: GitHub Actions release pipelines remain a supply-chain attack target
item.description: The guide surveys compromises involving projects such as tj-actions/changed-files, axios and LiteLLM, where attackers targeted release automation or its credentials. Its practical focus on hardening workflows is directly useful to teams shipping software through GitHub Actions.

item.title: Ubuntu CVE-2026-98432 remains unfixed nearly a week after disclosure
item.description: The Ask HN post says Ubuntu marks the CVE as severity 9.8 and lists a mitigation, but had not released a fix after nearly a week. The thread raises practical questions about OS patch pipelines and exposure during delays.

item.title: CAPTCHA field guide collects types, documented approaches and limitations
item.description: The reference organizes CAPTCHA families, their context, documented approaches and trade-offs, with an emphasis on authorized research. Engineers working on abuse prevention can use it as a starting point for comparing CAPTCHA mechanisms.

item.title: GitHub will block public pull_request_target workflows by default on December 2
item.description: GitHub plans to block these workflows in public repositories unless an Actions event policy allows them, extending protections against privileged workflows that can expose credentials. Maintainers need to review automation and configure exceptions before enforcement.

item.title: Composer 2.11 adds configurable delays for newly published dependencies
item.description: Composer's config.policy.cooldown setting delays new versions during dependency resolution, while leaving existing lockfile installs unaffected; Private Packagist can enforce the policy across teams. The feature gives PHP projects a native way to reduce exposure to freshly published malicious packages.

item.title: PHP2Shell research traces the exploit through PHP source code
item.description: The researcher says the walkthrough draws on PHP source analysis, experiments and investigations to explain how the vulnerabilities and exploitation process work. A source-level account can help security engineers understand exploit mechanics, though the excerpt gives no specific findings or remediation.

item.title: Alpine OpenSSH allows passwordless login under specific account conditions
item.description: A reachable Alpine SSH server can accept a long password for an account with no password set when another account has a certain password hash; updating and restarting OpenSSH, or disabling password logins, closes the hole. The report gives operators clear exposure conditions and mitigations.

item.title: Coldframe mimics supermarket fridge controllers to study exploit attempts
item.description: The one-file Python honeypot imitates Danfoss and Dixell interfaces, matching details such as headers and TLS versions, and recognizes several exploit attempts. It’s a concrete example of how to make a decoy convincing enough to observe attacks against industrial controls.

item.title: A musl crypt sentinel collision can give unauthenticated users shells on Alpine
item.description: On musl systems without PAM, an overlong password can hash to the same "*" used for locked accounts; sshd's timing-protection behavior can turn that collision into an unauthenticated shell. The Alpine exposure makes this a serious reminder that sentinel values can undermine authentication logic.

item.title: Attack on French bank via service provider enabled up to $133 million in transfers
item.description: An attack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa enabled fraudulent transactions, and the bank suspended some systems; reports put the potential theft at up to $133 million. The incident highlights how compromise involving a service provider can affect a major financial institution.

item.title: A crafted Android app can trigger a persistent crash loop during installation
item.description: A code-free app can crash a core Android process during installation, leaving a phone in a crash loop that may require a factory reset; deleting the file through ADB can help if debugging was already enabled. The report describes a severe failure mode in a widely deployed platform.

item.title: Post-quantum privacy work must extend beyond TLS to Privacy Pass
item.description: The excerpt explains how Privacy Pass uses unlinkable tokens for rate-limited site access and notes that quantum-vulnerable cryptography appears beyond TLS. Engineers planning cryptographic transitions should account for privacy protocols as well as transport security.

item.title: OpenBao 2.7 adds external keys, PostgreSQL read scaling and post-quantum algorithms
item.description: OpenBao 2.7 adds PostgreSQL read scaling, external HSM and KMS keys, post-quantum algorithms, and human review controls for sensitive operations. These changes matter to teams operating secrets infrastructure across scaled deployments.

item.title: An internet-wide scan finds services listening on TCP port 0
item.description: The author scanned IPv4 for TCP port 0, which applications can target on the wire even though operating systems use port 0 to request an ephemeral port. The findings may help engineers spot overlooked network exposure and gaps in scanning defaults.

item.title: CloneGuard scans repositories for credential-stealing tricks without running code
item.description: The dependency-free Go scanner reads project files without executing or installing them, looking for common malware tactics such as malicious install hooks and editor tasks. That read-only approach is relevant to securing developer workflows against supply-chain attacks.

item.title: curl will handle low- and medium-severity vulnerability reports publicly
item.description: curl is directing low- and medium-severity vulnerability reports to its public issue tracker instead of handling them under embargo, aiming to reduce pressure from private reports. The policy offers a concrete alternative for open-source security triage.

item.title: Pion makes its DTLS 1.3 implementation the default after 400 commits
item.description: After ten months and about 400 commits, Pion’s DTLS 1.3 implementation became the default, with a one-round-trip post-quantum key exchange, connection IDs, 0-RTT resumption and Encrypted Client Hello. The implementation story and interactive demos can help engineers understand the protocol’s practical trade-offs.

item.title: Xen fixes three use-after-free flaws across seven stable kernels
item.description: Three Xen use-after-free vulnerabilities can cause host-wide denial of service, and one may also permit privilege escalation; fixes are in seven stable kernel releases. Xen operators should upgrade to address risks at the hypervisor boundary.

item.title: OpenSSH workaround targets a critical flaw on Alpine Linux systems
item.description: The flaw affects Linux systems using musl libc with PAM disabled; OpenSSH recommends disabling password authentication or SSH, and Alpine plans to backport the fix to older releases. The precise configuration and immediate mitigation make this important for operators of affected hosts.

item.title: Binance attack shows signing services can misuse keys without extracting them
item.description: The attacker used stolen credentials and access to a wallet-signing service to obtain valid signatures, including an EIP-7702 standing delegation. Monitoring signature authority—not just transfers or key theft—can expose this class of risk.

item.title: 15,579 infected websites receive an estimated 135 million visits monthly
item.description: The report identifies 15,579 sites running malicious JavaScript, including credit-card skimmers and ClickFix lures, and estimates 135 million monthly visits. It highlights the scale of web compromise and the operational gap in notifying affected organizations.

item.title: Researchers find 820 restaurant impersonation domains used for payment skimming
item.description: Researchers found 820 domains impersonating 35 restaurant brands; some capture card details and request bank SMS verification codes. The campaign shows how cloned ordering sites can combine payment theft with account-verification scams.

item.title: glibc getaddrinfo accepts visually obscure Unicode forms of IPv4 addresses
item.description: A string containing unusual Unicode digits and invisible characters resolves through glibc 2.39 to the IPv4 address 69.30.206.130. Engineers validating or filtering addresses should account for how parsers interpret inputs that look unlike ordinary IP literals.

item.title: Kernel patch set aims to secure hibernation against tampering
item.description: A proposed lockdown fix addresses the risk that hibernation data can be tampered with, while also guarding against downgrade attacks using an older kernel. The design illustrates how adding security checks to a suspend-and-resume path introduces versioning challenges.

item.title: Fly.io patched its fleet for a Linux kernel bug in a 10-hour rollout
item.description: Fly.io explains how Linux checksum offload metadata applies to virtual networking and says it patched and rebooted its fleet over 10 hours. The account offers operational lessons for responding to kernel flaws across a cloud fleet.

item.title: Residential proxy exits appeared on the White House network 236 times
item.description: A proxy observatory recorded 236 exits across six addresses on 26 of 30 days, with 28 residential proxy services able to use the network; other services independently identified the addresses as proxy exits. It is useful security telemetry on proxy exposure in a high-profile network.

item.title: Alpine OpenSSH allows passwordless login under specific account conditions
item.description: A reachable Alpine SSH server can accept a 257–1024-byte password for an account marked with `*` if another account has a `$5$` or `$6$` hash; the advisory says to update and restart sshd or disable password authentication. The clear prerequisites and remediation make this useful for administrators of affected systems.

item.title: APT flaw lets a man-in-the-middle replace a package after verification
item.description: A redirect and resumed HTTP download can cause APT to merge downloads with the same URI, letting a man-in-the-middle replace a package after verification and execute code as root. The flaw affects a widely used package manager and merits prompt review of Debian's advisory.

item.title: Residential proxy services appear on White House network addresses
item.description: Security researchers reported persistent proxy activity from the Executive Office of the President’s network, including 236 observed exits and Windows devices running Infatica. The finding illustrates how consumer software can expose sensitive networks to third-party proxy traffic.

item.title: Linux patch targets privilege escapes across user-namespace boundaries
item.description: A patch series addresses cases where processes in a user namespace can elevate privileges for processes outside it. Container operators should care because this challenges the intended privilege boundary of user namespaces.

item.title: DNS-over-HTTPS exposed an ISP's rewritten DNS answers
item.description: Different answers from standard DNS and Cloudflare's DoH endpoint led the author to an IP owned by their ISP. The diagnostic is useful when debugging DNS failures and checking whether resolver traffic is being altered.

item.title: OpenSSH 10.6p2 adds an Alpine workaround as the team speeds up bug-fix releases
item.description: The release notice describes an Alpine workaround and says OpenSSH will issue more frequent releases as AI-assisted security reports increase. Operators should track updates to widely deployed SSH software, though the excerpt gives no details of the workaround.

item.title: Hackers remotely raised French blood-storage temperatures to 110°C
item.description: Attackers reportedly changed facility temperature settings remotely, and a technician detected the rise before it caused wider disruption or destroyed plasma. The incident highlights the stakes of securing and monitoring controls for operational systems.

item.title: Pwn.college offers free, hands-on cybersecurity training
item.description: The platform teaches core computing and cybersecurity through practical challenges and supports Arizona State University’s cybersecurity curriculum. Engineers can use it to build foundational security skills, though the excerpt gives few details about its exercises.

item.title: HTTP header injection can escalate to request desynchronization in one prompt
item.description: The described chain turns HTTP header injection into a CRLF-powered desynchronization that can redirect unrelated users, and PortSwigger has added a Burp AT scan check and skills for the technique. It gives testers a concrete exploitation path for a class of serious request-smuggling flaws.

item.title: A fake job interview led a Binance engineer to download malware before a $6.3B heist
item.description: Binance says attackers used fake interviews, malware, endpoint takeover and compromised internal AI tooling in the incident. The combination of social engineering and internal-tool compromise makes this a consequential security case for large engineering organizations.

item.title: APT download handling lets a man-in-the-middle replace a package and execute code as root
item.description: APT can merge downloads after an HTTP redirect and mishandle resumed downloads, letting an attacker replace a package after verification. The root-level consequence makes this a serious risk for systems that rely on APT.

item.title: Technical history challenges common cryptography backdoor conspiracy claims
item.description: The piece examines claims about NSA and NIST influence on cryptography standards against their history and technical arguments. Engineers choosing cryptographic standards can benefit from separating evidence-based scrutiny from assumptions about how backdoors work.

item.title: Electronic voting cryptography protects secrecy and verifiable tallies, but not every risk
item.description: The piece contrasts Helios for lower-risk settings with ElectionGuard's role as a cryptographic layer alongside paper-based election infrastructure. Engineers building high-stakes systems should account for operational safeguards beyond protocol guarantees.

item.title: Xbox 360 hypervisor exploit improves from 30% success to near 100%
item.description: The author says the Bad Update exploit went from about 20 minutes and a 30% success rate to near-instantaneous with near-100% success. It is a concise reverse-engineering update on an old console, with limited relevance beyond exploit-analysis techniques.

item.title: Google and partners dismantle XCPE botnet built into 1.3 million set-top boxes
item.description: The XCPE backdoor enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes, and operators sold access for ad fraud, residential proxies and malware deployment. The takedown highlights the risks of compromised devices shipped through an OEM supply chain.

item.title: Cloudflare launches Zero Wire vulnerability intelligence feed
item.description: Zero Wire is a public feed on Cloudflare Radar that briefs teams on critical vulnerabilities and helps them assess impact and response. It targets the triage burden that grows as AI speeds up vulnerability discovery.

item.title: Apple Watch features use ambient audio for transcripts and summaries
item.description: Live Rewind transcribes the previous 15 seconds of ambient audio, while Siri Recap summarizes conversations; Apple says audio is not stored and recaps are end-to-end encrypted. Engineers working on privacy-sensitive features should examine the stated safeguards and trade-offs.

item.title: Tests find smart-TV opt-out behavior varies by platform
item.description: Researchers ran 5,943 experiments across 12 TVs and found that opt-out behavior differed: some platforms stopped sending traffic, while only 60% of tested Samsung Tizen TVs showed a decrease or stop. The measurement is useful for evaluating privacy controls, though the findings concern consumer devices.

item.title: XCPE backdoor enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in a botnet
item.description: Google says the backdoor was built into multiple device models over several years and monetized through affiliate malware, including ad fraud and residential proxy enrollment. The case illustrates the supply-chain and infrastructure risks of compromised connected devices at scale.

item.title: LLM-jacking drove fraudulent cloud charges above $100,000 in a day
item.description: Mandiant reports attackers hijacking enterprise access to LLM providers, with individual incidents exceeding $100,000 in daily charges and some organizations reaching $1 million before revoking access. Teams operating model APIs need to treat credential theft as a direct inference-cost and incident-response risk.

item.title: Ubuntu LTS releases lack patched kernels for critical CVE-2026-98432
item.description: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04 reportedly have no patched kernel packages for CVE-2026-98432, leaving operators without an official update. Teams running those LTS kernels must weigh exposure against interim mitigations or moving workloads.

item.title: Ubuntu delays a patch for a remotely exploitable Linux TCP flaw
item.description: The post says a critical kernel TCP vulnerability has had a working root exploit, while Ubuntu had not shipped patches for supported releases. Patch delays in widely deployed server kernels can leave internet-facing systems exposed.

item.title: Cyberattacks switch supermarket freezer evaporators into defrost mode
item.description: A reported attack affected supermarkets in seven European countries by switching refrigeration evaporators into defrost mode, warming stock and forcing food to be discarded. It is a reminder that connected operational systems can turn a cyber incident into physical and supply-chain disruption.

item.title: AWS engineers examine how to manage the Linux kernel CVE flood
item.description: AWS engineers discuss keeping systems running and secure amid a surge of kernel CVE disclosures, finding that the advice to run current kernels works only partly. Operators responsible for large Linux fleets face the same tension between patch volume and maintaining service.

item.title: ChatGPT shared conversations enabled account takeover through script injection
item.description: A malicious public conversation could run attacker-controlled JavaScript in a signed-in ChatGPT session, read private conversation data and call authenticated APIs; the issue was fixed as P1. The exploit shows how shared content can become a high-impact account compromise on a widely used platform.

item.title: Multipath TCP use-after-free enables remote code execution on Linux
item.description: A race involving a retransmitted SYN can free a connection options structure while another thread uses it, enabling kernel memory disclosure or attacker-controlled writes; Go enables multipath TCP by default. Systems with MPTCP listeners should apply their distribution's kernel patch.

item.title: Hackers exploit digital-ad-screen software to hijack billboards across several countries
item.description: A hacking group claims an exploit in digital advertising software let it access display systems in several countries, after an automated scan found thousands of exposed systems. The incident highlights the security risks of connected commercial infrastructure.

item.title: Two critical PHP remote-code-execution flaws require exposure checks and patching
item.description: Unit 42 reports two PHP remote-code-execution vulnerabilities rated 9.2 and urges users to assess exposure and patch. PHP’s broad use across web servers and content-management systems makes the advisory relevant to many production environments.

item.title: GitHub Actions hardening narrows, but does not eliminate, pwn request paths
item.description: GitHub’s 2026 changes add checkout protections, read-only cache tokens, and event policies, while remaining risks include explicit opt-ins, outdated checkout versions, unprotected triggers, and script injection. The audit checklist can help teams reassess CI workflows that handle untrusted pull requests.

item.title: arm64e pointer authentication protects control flow with hardware-verified codes
item.description: On arm64e, pointers carry cryptographic codes that hardware checks at branches, with verification keys kept out of memory; the post says attacks instead target modifiers, signing operations, or crashes. The design shows how hardware-backed control-flow protections change kernel attack paths.

item.title: Trigger.dev says an attack exposed some customers’ environment variables
item.description: Trigger.dev says an attacker gained unauthorized access to environment variables at a subset of organizations, and that it blocked the exploit and contacted affected owners. The notice highlights the impact of secrets exposure in a multi-tenant service.

item.title: Six of eight tested SVG sanitizers can be bypassed to execute JavaScript
item.description: The tests bypassed six popular SVG sanitizers and describe JavaScript execution in Firefox via a response header, plus Safari importing a GIF as SVG. Teams accepting SVG uploads should review their sanitization and browser-handling assumptions.

item.title: Email encryption protects against different threats in different ways
item.description: The guide distinguishes email threats such as account compromise, network interception and data breaches, and notes that encryption methods have different trade-offs. It offers useful security context, though it is aimed at general email users rather than systems engineers.

item.title: ACLs lose authorization context across messages, enabling web attacks
item.description: The excerpt argues that ACLs cannot make correct decisions involving more than two principals because message sends discard needed information, linking the flaw to clickjacking and CSRF. It offers a useful security-model lesson for engineers designing authorization across interacting services.

item.title: VOLTA infostealer uses LLMs to rank stolen assets by victim value
item.description: VOLTA sends stolen credentials, sessions, and wallet evidence to an LLM for monetization ranking, then falls back to a three-model chain if a model refuses. It shows how attackers can turn model access and guardrail failures into a post-theft analysis pipeline.

item.title: ChatGPT sandbox message handling enabled account-takeover attacks
item.description: A sandboxed HTML preview could message a parent page handler that used innerHTML, enabling HTML injection and an unsandboxed iframe despite CSP restrictions. The exploit chain shows how cross-frame messaging can undermine isolation in a major AI product.

item.title: Linux TCP use-after-free affects stable kernels and can be reached remotely
item.description: A remote unauthenticated IPv4 TCP handshake reaches a use-after-free; fixed stable-kernel versions are listed, while Ubuntu and RHEL still showed affected packages. Linux operators should check distro advisories and patch, especially with MPTCP listeners.

item.title: An Intel Hyper-Threading cache side channel enabled RSA key recovery
item.description: The cache-state leak between simultaneous threads yielded a proof of concept that recovered enough RSA private-key bits to reconstruct the key. It shows how shared hardware can undermine cryptographic isolation.

item.title: Savannah email parsing flaw could have enabled Bash repository takeover
item.description: A crafted email address gave a registered user code execution, superuser access and a path to add an SSH key to Bash’s upstream repository. The chain shows how a forge compromise can become a software supply-chain risk.

item.title: RAMBO uses memory-bus signals to leak data from air-gapped computers
item.description: The paper says malware can generate radio signals from RAM and encode files, keystrokes, biometric data or encryption keys. It highlights that physical network isolation does not prevent every covert channel from compromised hardware.

item.title: Molly remains exposed to fixes already shipped in mainline Signal
item.description: Molly’s latest release is listed as July 31, while mainline Signal 8.27.1 includes fixes for an exploit Molly reportedly still exposes. Users of this Signal fork may need to switch until updates resume.
